explanations.b: Correct. Gene Amdahl presented the law in 1967.

questions.question: Q2 What does Amdahl's Law describe?

answers.b: The theoretical limit of speedup from parallelization

explanations.b: Correct. It describes the maximum speedup achievable by adding more processors.

questions.question: Q3 If 90% of a program is parallelizable, what is the maximum speedup with infinite processors?
Q4 What is the 'serial fraction' of a workload?

answers.a: The part that runs on the network
answers.b: The part that cannot be parallelized
answers.c: The part that uses the most memory

explanations.b: Correct. The serial fraction must execute sequentially, limiting parallel speedup.

questions.question: Q5 What does 'diminishing returns' mean in parallel computing?

answers.a: Each additional processor adds less speedup than the previous one

explanations.a: Correct. Beyond a point, adding more processors provides minimal benefit.

answers.b: Additional time spent on inter-node synchronization and data exchange
answers.c: The power consumed by network cables

explanations.b: Correct. Communication overhead represents the time cost of coordination between processors.

Q8 What happens when communication overhead exceeds the benefit of adding more nodes?

explanations.b: Correct. When overhead > benefit, adding nodes can actually slow down the system.

questions.question: Q9 Why is Amdahl's Law important for data center budgeting?

answers.b: It helps identify the optimal number of nodes before returns diminish

explanations.b: Correct. Understanding scaling limits prevents overspending on hardware that provides no benefit.

questions.question: Q10 In the extended model, what does Co × ln(N) represent?

answers.b: Communication overhead that grows logarithmically with node count

explanations.b: Correct. The ln(N) term models how communication costs grow with system size.
